notes.1: Written in Ionic Greek with many slips. The verb of 1 is lost. In 7 the papyrus has ‘in Poserapi’, translated as ‘with Oserapis’. ‘Funeral offerings’ (2) renders the partly restored κτερέων.

nodes.text: O lord Oserapis and gods who [sit] with Oserapis, [...] to you, Artemisie,
daughter of Amasis, against the father of the daughter, [who] deprived [her] of the funeral offerings
and of the tomb. If, then, he has not done what is just by me and by his own children,
just as indeed he has done what is unjust to me and to his own children, may Oserapis and the gods grant him
not to obtain a tomb from his children, nor himself to bury his own parents. And while
the complaint lies here, may he perish miserably, both on land and at sea, both he himself
and his possessions, at the hands of Oserapis and the gods who sit in [the shrine of] Oserapis,
and may he not find Oserapis gracious, nor the gods [who] with Oserapis
sit. Artemisie has laid down this supplication, beseeching
Oserapis to judge the case, [and] the gods who sit with Oserapis.
And while the supplication [lies] here, may he in no way find the gods gracious,
the father of the girl. And whoever [removes] these letters and wrongs Artemisie,
